title: HE SLIPPED AWAY.
paragraphs: HE SLIPPED AWAY.

Not from pressure.
Not from people.
Not from purpose.
From applause.
Crowds were exploding around Jesus Christ.

The sick were lining the streets.
Demons were screaming.
Leprosy was vanishing from skin like mist under the morning sun.
Power was everywhere.
But something strange kept happening.

Right when the crowds got bigger…
Right when His name spread louder…
He disappeared.
Scripture whispers the moment:
“But Jesus often withdrew to lonely places and prayed.” — Luke 5:16
Often.

Not occasionally.
Not when convenient.
Often.
Think about the tension.

People were desperate for Him.
Miracles were multiplying.
Momentum was building.
If this were modern ministry, the advice would be clear:

Stay visible.
Keep the crowds.
Build the platform.
But Jesus slipped away.
Because public power is born in private surrender.

Before the miracles…
there was silence.

Before the authority…
there was intimacy.

Before the crowds…
there was a lonely hillside where the Son spoke with the Father.
Imagine the scene.

The night air cool against His skin.
Dust clinging to His robe from a long day of healing.
Stars burning quietly above Judea.
No applause.
No disciples.
Just the Son of God whispering to the Father who sent Him.
Not performing.
Communing.
Here is the scandal most people miss:
The One with all power still prayed.
If anyone could skip prayer, it was Him.
Yet Jesus Christ chose dependence.
Why?
Because the Kingdom doesn’t run on human strength.
It runs on surrender.
And this exposes something in us.

We rush to platforms.
We chase influence.
We want impact.
But we avoid the lonely place.

The quiet room.
The kneeling moment.
The honest prayer where pride dies and the heart becomes small again before God.
But the Gospel begins there.
Not with strong people.
With broken ones.
With sinners who realize they cannot fix themselves.
That is why Jesus came.
He did not come merely to teach prayer.
He came to carry our sin to the cross.
At Golgotha, the sinless Son took the weight of every hidden failure, every secret shame.
Then three days later, the grave lost its grip.
Because grace had the final word.
So when we slip away to pray, we are not climbing toward God.
We are responding to a door Jesus already opened.
Through His blood.
Through His resurrection.
Through His mercy that still reaches the quiet corners of our lives.
Maybe the power you’re asking God for…
is waiting in the prayer you keep postponing.
Slip away.
Close the door.
Whisper His name.
And watch what God does with a heart that chooses the lonely place.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
